Title: Narrative is the recurrent failure point — target Narrative to preserve a company-first story
Description: Across multiple experiments the first visible editorial hierarchy break most often appears in the Narrative stage: Narrative frequently reframes a company-first brief into a product/orchestration-first story or introduces unsupported audience/validation language. Use the Narrative stage as the controlled intervention point in the next trial to test whether preserving the company→product relationship at Narrative reduces downstream drift.
Audience: Prompt engineers, workflow architects, content editors, experiment designers responsible for the Nuëyon.Compose pipeline
Rationale: The Narrative stage is where high-impact editorial decisions (story selection, hook, audience framing) are applied. The report shows Narrative is the most recurrent locus of the earliest observable hierarchy shift, so an upstream trial that explicitly constrains or reworks Narrative inputs offers the strongest, highest-evidence path to improving company-first introductions without inventing root-cause explanations.
Evidence: Facts: the report's cross-experiment localization lists Narrative as the first visible hierarchy shift in many runs (Experiment 007 candidates 001–002; Experiment 008 A-002; Experiment 009 baseline 002/003 and Candidate runs 001–003). The 'Cross-experiment patterns' section explicitly states: 'Narrative is the most recurrent first visible hierarchy shift in the available records.' Supporting examples: Experiment 007 Candidate 001 — Synthesis kept Nuëyon/Compose primary but Narrative turned orchestration into the through-line; Experiment 009 Baseline 002 — Narrative made orchestration the 'immediate, directional focus' and Compose then escalated it. Interpretation: this pattern makes Narrative the highest-leverage control point for preventing downstream reframing. Gaps and uncertainty: Narrative is the most frequent observable locus but not the sole cause (some runs show Idea or Synthesis drift first). The report does not prove causation; a controlled trial (as recommended) is required to confirm whether constraining Narrative reduces overall pipeline drift.
